steps_title: How the AI part number search works
steps_subtitle: Three steps, a few minutes, no account to create.
step1_title: Give the brand and serial number
step1_desc: They are on the engine's ID plate. Then describe the part in your own words: impeller, spark plug, anode, carburetor kit…
step2_desc: The serial number is matched against the brand's plate pattern to find the exact model, its family and its catalog code.
step3_desc: The OEM part number comes from a sourced database, with its source and verification date. Otherwise, a direct link to your model's exploded view.
parts_title: The engine parts the assistant can
parts_subtitle: The parts catalog covers outboards and inboard diesels, assembly by assembly: fuel system, ignition, cooling, lower unit, exhaust… Click a part to start your search.
part1_desc: The number one wear part on an outboard: impeller, full pump kit, housing gasket — the part number depends on the exact model code.
part2_title: Spark plugs, coil and CDI unit
part2_desc: Ignition coil, charge coil, pulser coil, CDI unit, stop switch: the whole ignition assembly.
part3_desc: Block, lower unit, heat exchanger or saildrive anode: the right shape and alloy for your model.
part4_desc: Repair kit, float chamber gasket, needle valve, main and pilot jets, float, pilot screw.
part5_title: Fuel filter, diaphragm and primer bulb
part5_desc: Fuel pump kit, diaphragm, filter, primer bulb, tank connector: the complete fuel system.
part6_desc: Thermostat, head gasket, gasket set, piston rings: the power unit parts, outboard and inboard alike.
part7_desc: Gearcase seal kit, drain screw gasket, propeller, nut and washer: the lower unit and propulsion.
part8_desc: Exhaust elbow and gasket, waterlock, injectors, primary water separator, lift pump, sterndrive bellows, saildrive diaphragm.
faq_q1: Is the part number search really free and account-free?
faq_a1: Yes. You get {count} free searches without creating an account, straight from this page. No credit card, no sign-up.
faq_q2: Which engines and brands are covered?
faq_a2: Outboards and inboard diesels from the brands in the FleetAi engine catalog (Yamaha, Mercury…). If your brand is not recognised you can still describe the part: the assistant points you to the retailer catalogs.
faq_q3: Where do the part numbers come from? Can the AI be wrong?
faq_a3: The AI never invents a number: a displayed part number comes exclusively from our sourced database, with its source and verification date. When it has none, it says so and sends you to your model's exploded view. Always check the part number before ordering.
faq_q4: What if my engine is not identified?
faq_a4: Read the serial number and model code on the engine's ID plate (under the cowling or on the bracket) and search again. Otherwise the assistant gives you the retailer catalogs where that code opens the exploded view.
faq_q5: What happens after my {count} free searches?
faq_a5: Create your free FleetAi account (Starter plan): your engines are saved once and for all and you get the parts catalog assembly by assembly. Pro and Enterprise plans add the AI assistant with no conversation cap.
faq_q6: Where do I order the part once I have the number?
faq_a6: From the retailer of your choice. The suggested links (Partzilla, Boats.net, Crowley Marine…) open your model's exploded view; prices shown there are indicative. FleetAi does not sell parts.
